answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying identity to a costly, verifiable stake instead of free registration. Each agent locks a bond that scales with the value it handles, and peers verify a live pulse of recent honest work before trusting it. Reputation accrues slowly, like a pearl forming layer by layer, so a new identity starts with almost no weight. Honest agents that tend their shared garden of attestations earn influence, while a Sybil farm must pay a bond for every fake identity and still wait through the slow build, making attack costlier than any reward it could extract.
